messages:
sasha: FYI saw a burst of reconnects for /v1/stream in eu-central right after yesterday's proxy canary (22:05 UTC). Clients report a sudden 204 and then immediate reconnect. console shows session_closed spike but it's lumped as 'unexpected'. cc @akhil @jamal
akhil: SSE or WS? any pattern in user-agents?
sasha: SSE. Mostly our long-lived SDKs and some older mobile clients. UA sample: RedwoodStream/1.4.2 and okhttp/3.12.
jamal: I pulled packet traces from the edge. Proxy is returning 204 keepalive on idle and then closing socket. The runtime also emits a client_close shortly after which the console aggregates into a single counter so we can't tell which side initiated the close. That makes the UI useless for this.
elsa: Could be the new idle threshold in the canary (was 120s -> 40s). Proxy emits a 204 path to push clients to reconnect. For some clients (esp mobile) reconnect -> backoff -> new session -> duplicate subscription during resume window. Billing and telemetry double counts.
infra-bot: Alert: stream.sessions_closed_rate /v1/stream eu-central exceeded 2.8x baseline (22:06-22:20). Incident I-9321 created.
jamal: We should add explicit ingest tags: close_kind={proxy_204|client_reset|runtime_close}, route_config_version, and session_sticky=true/false. That lets the console split the spikes.
akhil: Agree. I'll add a low-card metric `stream.close_kind` via counter with tag close_kind and route_version. Keep cardinality small.
elsa: Operationally, we need a runtime flag to make fallback routing a no-op for streaming endpoints during canaries. The fallback currently triggers when route latency > threshold and will re-route in-flight resumables; that multiplies side-effects. Proposal: annotate route with `no-fallback-during-rollout=true` or a per-route sticky-session TTL.
jamal: I can prototype a feature-flag: `streaming.sticky_sessions=true` with TTL in ms. Example patch I used locally: 
```
PATCH /config/routes/streaming
{ "sticky_sessions_ms": 120000, "allow_cross_region_fallback": false }
```
elsa: Nice. That would keep resume tokens bound to the same shard for TTL and avoid double-sends.
sasha: Ops asked for quick numbers so they can decide whether to rollback canary. rough impact?
Nina: ~1.7k affected sessions in eu-central over 15m, peak reconnect rate +5.2%, estimated duplicate session opens ~320, token churn ~0.9% for that route. Not large cluster-wide but noticeable for high-throughput customers.
akhil: Hotfix options: 1) increase proxy idle window to previous value on canary nodes, 2) enable sticky_sessions feature-flag for /v1/stream in canary, 3) add a console annotation showing route idle_ms and route_version. I prefer (2) + (3) for short term.
jamal: I rolled sticky_sessions=true to canary pool and disabled cross-region fallback for streaming routes. Watchlist configured.
canary-bot: Rollout update: canary/proxy-config+sticky v2026-03-22-22:40 applied to eu-central canary group (node-pool c5-stream-1).
elsa: Also changing console: add a tiny UI pill that surfaces `route_idle_ms` and `route_config` for the selected timeframe. On-call shouldn't need to hunt infra YAMLs.
akhil: Will open PRs: telemetry#445 (close_kind metric), console#1129 (route pill), infra#780 (sticky flag rollout).
sasha: Thanks. Also consider adding a client-visible header `X-Stream-Grace: <ms>` so clients can be graceful and backoff less aggressively when they see short idle windows. Could help mobile SDKs.
jamal: Good idea. We'll add header emission behind feature flag.
elsa: For follow-up, let's add a one-paragraph playbook entry under ops/streaming: how to triage proxy-induced 204s, which metrics to check, and immediate mitigations.
sasha: I'll draft the playbook. If metrics stabilize by 23:10 UTC we won't rollback. tagging @nina for customer comms.
Nina: I'll prepare a short status note for affected customers and ops.
sasha: Closing once alerts quiet. Thanks everyone.
